# Laycal

> Laycal is a speed-to-lead platform. When someone submits a business's form, an AI voice agent phones them within a minute, asks the business's qualifying questions, handles objections and books the meeting on the business's calendar.

## Key facts

- What it does: places an outbound phone call to each new lead within a minute of the form being submitted, qualifies the lead and books a meeting during the call.
- Who it is for: any business where the first company to call usually wins the customer, for example home services (HVAC, plumbing, roofing, electrical), e-commerce with considered purchases, and B2B.
- Lead sources: website forms, Google Forms, ad lead forms and CRMs, by sending each new lead to Laycal as it arrives. A CSV can be uploaded for an existing list.
- Calendar: Google Calendar. The agent offers only free slots and creates the event while the lead is on the phone.
- After each call: the outcome, a recording, a written summary and the details captured (name, email, appointment time).
- Phone numbers: works with the business's own Twilio, Plivo or Vonage numbers.
- Languages: English, Spanish, French and German.
- Concurrency: many calls can run at the same time, so a busy hour does not create a backlog.
- Pricing: pay as you go, per calling minute. No seats, plans or monthly minimum. The rate is confirmed on a demo.
- Access: invite-only. There is no public sign-up or free trial; accounts are created by invitation after a demo.
- Second use, lead reactivation: Laycal can call a list of past leads the business already holds and book the ones who are still interested. Lists must be opted-in; consent and do-not-call compliance are the customer's responsibility.

## What Laycal is not

- It does not answer inbound phone calls. It is not an AI receptionist or an answering service.
- It is not a dialer or phone system for a team of sales reps.
- It is not a cold-calling tool. It calls people who asked to be contacted.
- It does not source leads or send email or SMS sequences.
